_comment: Long TTS dictations (50-80 s at 150 words per minute) for the parakeet_mlx incremental-decoding bench. `say` reads `spoken`; `ref` is the text the user wants. `concat` clips join others' texts (one long dictation). Terms come from ../parakeet-mlx-boost/terms.json.

clips.spoken: Okay, so I looked at the pull request for the session store refactor. The main change moves the state from the old context provider into use session store, and that part looks fine to me. What worries me is the migration in session store dot ts, because it reads the old key from local storage and never deletes it, so after a few releases we will have two copies of every session on disk. I would also like a test for the case where the stored value is not valid JSON, since that is exactly what happened last week when a user downgraded. Before you merge, please run basedpyright and ruff on the whole repository, not only on the files you touched, and make sure cargo clippy is clean on the Rust side as well. One more thing: the timeout in the retry loop is still hard coded. Move it into the config file next to the other network settings and document the default in the readme. If all of that is done by Thursday, we can ship it with the next release and mention it in the changelog.

clips.spoken: Here is what I found while debugging the cluster this morning. First, I ran kubectl get pods in the default namespace, and two of the workers were stuck in a crash loop. The logs showed that the container could not reach the database, so I checked the network policy, and it was blocking traffic from the new subnet. After I added the subnet to the allow list, the pods came back, but the latency on the API was still about twice as high as yesterday. It turned out that the connection pool was set to five, which is far too low for the load we see in the afternoon. I raised it to fifty, and the tail latency dropped by more than half. Next week I want to set up an alert for pool saturation, and I also want to move the whole thing behind Tailscale, so that we stop exposing the admin port to the internet. Let me know if you see anything else that looks odd in the dashboards.

clips.spoken: I have been using hark for a few days now on Hyprland and on the Mac, and overall the accuracy is much better than I expected. The biggest win is that it picks up the names from the repository, so when I say parse CLI args or use effect, it actually writes the identifier instead of random words. The part that still bothers me is the delay when I talk for a long time. If I dictate a whole paragraph, I have to wait two or three seconds before anything appears, and that breaks my flow. Short commands feel instant, which is great. I would also like the filler words to disappear in chat, but in the terminal I want exactly what I said, no more and no less. Another small thing is that two dictations in a row get glued together without a space, so I end up fixing the text by hand. If those three issues were fixed, I would switch from Superwhisper completely.
